elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14 (unchanged) presupposes and gives effect to a unilateral Client exit: "TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement." No cause is required, so a Customer convenience right exists in substance (the deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' probe fails only because the clause never uses the phrase 'for convenience'/'without cause').

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 runs service to "the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides ... notice", i.e. an effective notice period of roughly 31–61 days, not a fixed period of 30 days or fewer. No edit shortens it.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 13 nor Section 14 as rendered contains any refund of prepaid fees; the redline adds none. Monthly arrears billing is asserted in the rationale but is not operative refund language.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: TrueLink's only no-cause exit in Section 13 is notice of intent not to renew, effective at the end of the then-current one-year period; the Section 13 proviso terminating Sections 2 and 3 is triggered only by Client breach/default (for cause), not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14 gives Client a no-cause termination taking effect on the last day of the month following the notice month (approx. 31–61 days), which is at or shorter than the fallback's 60–90 day window and therefore satisfies the fallback ceiling in the customer-favourable direction; the existing language is retained unchanged.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated-fee obligation appears in the rendered termination/term provisions, so a cap is inapplicable; Client's only post-termination obligations are the transition duties (new name server within 30 days, new hosting environment within 60 days), which are not fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 13 permits TrueLink a no-cause exit solely by delivering "notice of intent not to renew" before "the end of said year"; there is no mid-term vendor convenience right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Edited Section 13: "unless Client delivers written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days, or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year" — TrueLink's notice must be delivered at least 90 days before expiry.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred-level requirement; listed for completeness. The preferred level instead bars any vendor convenience right during the committed term, which Section 13 as rendered satisfies.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the single edit raises TrueLink's non-renewal notice to ninety (90) days, curing the walk-away trigger (vendor convenience exit on fewer than 90 days' notice), while the pre-existing Client exit in Section 14 and the end-of-term-only limit on TrueLink's exit already satisfy the other three fallback elements.

Preferred is not reached: Client's notice period effectively runs 31–61 days (last day of the month following the notice month) rather than 30 days or fewer, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is added. This is correctly treated as a rationale note rather than a further redline, since the fallback is met on its material terms.

Minimal: one asymmetric split of the existing mutual non-renewal notice sentence; no survival tails, refund mechanics, expense language or other extras were added, and Client's favourable 30-day non-renewal notice and Section 14 exit are retained verbatim.

Intent preserved: "such notice" unambiguously refers back to the immediately preceding "written notice of intent not to renew"; the "prior to the end of said year" tail still governs both notices; the pre-existing (and unaltered) internal reference to Section 12 for termination remains as in the original document and is not made worse by the edit.

Drafting nit (not a defect requiring repair): the reliance on Section 14's oblique phrasing means the agreement never states expressly that Client may terminate without cause. If the counterparty later argues Section 14 is only a wind-down timing provision, the fallback's first element would be at risk; a short clarifying phrase ("Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, in which case ...") would remove that ambiguity without exceeding the checklist.
